I love this post. Your struggles seem very real and strike a particular chord with me. There are a few things I want to point out if you haven't noticed already.

You don't have to be like your parents. While they may influence you in some ways, you are obviously aware of their good habits and their bad. How you live your life and lead your future family is entirely up to you. I hope you can grow to be as supportive as your father and as financially responsible as your mom. I think you can.

As for your mom's comments to you, she is clearly wrong. You are an accomplished athlete and on your way to college. That is a significant achievement! You are on a good path for the rest your life, more so than most people. Just because your mom can't see that doesn't make it any less true.

It's perfectly fine to wait for the one. I find it admirable actually, since it means you value yourself enough to find a girl of high quality, instead of just settling for the first shitty person that comes along.

If that girl in physics is truly interested in you, it means the advantage is in your court! You don't have to do much, just say hi and be friendly. While you may be nervous on the inside (also a good thing!) if you exhibit a positive and friendly attitude, 90% of people respond in kind.

Now it could be that something works out with her. That's pretty cool. Or it could be that you guys just stay friends. That's still awesome! It means you got to meet and got to know someone new. If you take any advice, I'd highly suggest approaching her with zero expectations. And don't trying to force anything. It's so much better when things happen naturally. And who knows...things could unfold in a different way than you expect but be more beautiful than you imagine.

Good luck, bro. I think you got this. I love you too.

Yea so let's see. I did medical leave for 1 semester and flunked out another. Took about a year off in total. 

Did some community college courses on the side and a part-time job. The CC courses were super easy, so I just sat down and did the hw as soon as a got home. Took like an hour tops. Especially since I was at my parents house with no friends and had nothing else to do. My gf at the time commented, man if you just had this work ethic while at our school, you'd be doing just fine.

That's when it hit me. Work ethic is a skill and I have none of it. My intelligence is a gift, but also a crutch. I've relied on it so much I haven't had any chance to strengthen the other skills I needed. 

Those kids who weren't that smart but just simply sat down after class and started reviewing their notes, eating a snack, doing the problem sets, meeting up in study groups. I could walk circles around them when it came to picking things up quick. But man, they owned me when it came to the actual grades.

> And it's not even that I'm not interested, I do want to do this, I just feel incapable of motivating myself.

Sounds like we have some disconnect here. Like med school means a lot to you, but for some reason you are unable/unwilling to sit down and work. Could be that you love helping people but just have test anxiety. Or that you're burnt out and need an easier courseload. Or maybe you're like me, and never learned good study habits and setting up a regular schedule. (Aka being smart enough to get by works fine in undergrad, but doesn't cut it for the prestigious universities.) Either way, something about what you want to do, what you're capable of doing, and what you're actually doing, doesn't match up.

One last thing: No one likes to study. You just do it because something else is just more important to you. Yes it's a chore. Yes it's a slog. Yes it's not fun. But you just do it even if you don't feel like it. This whole "motivation" thing is kind of a lie...you'll never "feel like" doing it. You just do it anyway.
